claims.claim: Fluorescent signal was observed in H2BC11, ACTB, TUBA1B, ANLN, RHOA, KRT18, SOX2, NES, and TUBB3-tagged populations.
claims.source: As expected for genes that are expressed in iPSCs, we observed a fluorescent signal in H2BC11, ACTB, TUBA1B, ANLN, RHOA, KRT18, SOX2, NES, and TUBB3-tagged populations (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B–T).
claims.evidence: This is shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B–T with flow cytometry data.

claims.claim: The mean fluorescence intensity of tagged cells correlated well with their expected relative expression levels.
claims.source: For these proteins, the mean fluorescence intensity of tagged cells correlated well with their expected relative expression levels (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A and U).
claims.evidence: This is shown by comparing Figure 2—figure supplement 1A (RNA-seq data) and Figure 2—figure supplement 1U (fluorescence intensity).

claims.claim: E-cadherin-mNG211 was enriched at cell junctions.

claims.evidence: This is shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1W–X with microscopy images.

claims.claim: An average recovery of 61.4% was achieved for single-cell clones in 96-well plates across five genes.

claims.claim: Isolated clones had diverse genotypes with alleles containing mNG211, mutated mNG211, indel mutations, and WT sequences.
claims.source: We found that clones had diverse genotypes with alleles containing mNG211, mutated mNG211, indel mutations, and WT sequences (Figure 3B).
claims.evidence: This is shown in Figure 3B with genotyping data from Nanopore sequencing.

claims.claim: Both homozygous and heterozygous clones were obtained for smNG2-anillin and smNG2-RhoA.

claims.evidence: This is shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1H–I with fluorescence intensity measurements.

claims.claim: Homozygous clones for anillin and RhoA were brighter than heterozygous clones.
claims.source: We obtained both homozygous and heterozygous clones carrying smNG2-anillin and smNG2-RhoA, and we found homozygous clones that were brighter than heterozygous ones (Figure 3—figure supplement 1H–I).
claims.evidence: This is shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1H–I with fluorescence intensity measurements.

claims.claim: The complementation between mNG21-10 and mNG211 occurs efficiently over a range of mNG211 expression levels.
claims.source: This suggests that the complementation between mNG21-10 and mNG211 occurs efficiently over a range of mNG211 expression, since anillin is expressed weakly and RhoA is expressed more strongly in iPSCs.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the observation that both weakly and strongly expressed proteins show efficient complementation.

claims.claim: H2B was nuclear during interphase and localized to condensed chromatin during mitosis in the final tagged cell lines.
claims.source: Consistent with the expected localization for these proteins, H2B was nuclear during interphase and localized to condensed chromatin during mitosis, actin was cortical in both interphase and mitotic cells, tubulin was cytosolic during interphase and localized to mitotic spindles, anillin was nuclear during interphase and enriched in the cleavage furrow during cytokinesis, and RhoA was cytosolic during interphase and cortically enriched during mitosis.

claims.claim: iPSCs stopped dividing and detached from the coverslip after a few minutes of imaging using standard optical settings.
claims.source: After a few minutes of imaging using standard optical settings, iPSCs stopped dividing and detached from the coverslip, independently of laser wavelength (data not shown), suggesting that iPSCs are more sensitive to photo-toxicity than transformed and cancerous cell lines.

claims.claim: iPSCs are more sensitive to photo-toxicity than transformed and cancerous cell lines.
claims.source: After a few minutes of imaging using standard optical settings, iPSCs stopped dividing and detached from the coverslip, independently of laser wavelength (data not shown), suggesting that iPSCs are more sensitive to photo-toxicity than transformed and cancerous cell lines.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the observation that iPSCs stopped dividing during imaging.

claims.claim: The signal-to-noise ratio was low for H2B, α-tubulin, anillin, and RhoA in images acquired with low-exposure settings.

claims.evidence: This is shown in Figure 4A with signal-to-noise ratio measurements.

claims.claim: A CARE neural network was trained on sets of matched high- and low-exposure images for each cell line.
claims.source: We trained a CARE (Content-Aware image REstoration) neural network on sets of matched high- and low-exposure images for each cell line (Figure 4B; Weigert et al., 2018), and used the trained model to restore timelapse movies acquired with low-exposure settings (Figure 4C–G).

claims.claim: The signal-to-noise ratio was drastically improved for timelapse images of H2B, α-tubulin, anillin, and RhoA after CARE restoration.
claims.source: The signal-to-noise ratio was drastically improved for timelapse images of H2B, α-tubulin, anillin, and RhoA (Figure 4C–G).
claims.evidence: This is shown in Figure 4C–G with comparisons of raw and restored images.

claims.claim: The duration of contractile ring ingression in anillin-tagged iPSCs is 18.6±4.0 min.
claims.source: First we measured the duration of contractile ring ingression in anillin-tagged iPSCs (18.6±4.0 min; Figure 5B).
claims.evidence: This is shown in Figure 5B with timing measurements.

claims.claim: In metaphase iPSCs, anillin is cytosolic, RhoA is weakly enriched at the cortex, and actin is strongly enriched at the cortex.
claims.source: In metaphase cells, we found that anillin is cytosolic, while RhoA is weakly enriched at the cortex and actin is strongly enriched at the cortex (Figures 4C, D, G ,, 5C).

claims.claim: Anillin accumulates at the equatorial cortex ~4 min after anaphase onset in iPSCs.
claims.source: During mitotic exit, anillin accumulates at the equatorial cortex ~4 min after anaphase onset, while RhoA accumulates by ~6 min, and actin remains strongly cortical with some equatorial enrichment by ~4–5 min (Figures 4C, D, G ,, 5D).
claims.evidence: This is shown in Figures 4C, D, G and 5D with timelapse imaging data.

claims.claim: RhoA accumulates at the equatorial cortex ~6 min after anaphase onset in iPSCs.
claims.source: During mitotic exit, anillin accumulates at the equatorial cortex ~4 min after anaphase onset, while RhoA accumulates by ~6 min, and actin remains strongly cortical with some equatorial enrichment by ~4–5 min (Figures 4C, D, G ,, 5D).
claims.evidence: This is shown in Figures 4C, D, G and 5D with timelapse imaging data.

claims.claim: Anillin forms a narrow peak at the onset of ingression (4.1±0.7 μm) in iPSCs.

claims.evidence: This is shown in Figure 5E–F with breadth measurements.

claims.claim: RhoA localizes more broadly at the onset of ingression (6.6±2.2 μm) compared to anillin in iPSCs.
claims.source: We then measured the breadth of cortically enriched anillin and RhoA at the onset of ingression and found that anillin forms a narrow peak (4.1±0.7 μm), while RhoA localizes more broadly (6.6±2.2 μm; Figure 5E–F).
claims.evidence: This is shown in Figure 5E–F with breadth measurements.

claims.claim: iPSCs have a poorly-organized central spindle in anaphase.
claims.source: We found that cells have a poorly-organized central spindle in anaphase (Figure 5G–H), and the astral microtubules appear to contact the equatorial cortex (Figure 5G).
claims.evidence: This is shown in Figure 5G–H with microscopy images and intensity measurements.

claims.claim: Astral microtubules appear to contact the equatorial cortex in iPSCs during anaphase.
claims.source: We found that cells have a poorly-organized central spindle in anaphase (Figure 5G–H), and the astral microtubules appear to contact the equatorial cortex (Figure 5G).
claims.evidence: This is shown in Figure 5G with microscopy images.

claims.claim: Anillin-tagged iPSCs completed ingression faster than HepG2 and HEK293 cells, slower than HCT116 cells, and similar to HeLa cells.
claims.source: We found that anillin-tagged iPSCs completed ingression in 18.6±4.0 min; faster than HepG2 and HEK293 cells, slower than HCT116 cells, and similar to HeLa cells (Figure 5B; Husser et al., 2022).

claims.claim: The weak central spindle in anaphase iPSCs may explain the broad localization of RhoA.
claims.source: Thus, the weak central spindle in anaphase iPSCs may explain the broad localization of RhoA (Figure 5G–H).
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the observation of the weak central spindle and broad RhoA localization.

claims.claim: Perturbations that weaken the central spindle in HeLa cells result in more diffuse Ect2-Cyk4 complexes and a broader zone of active RhoA.

claims.claim: The 201B7 smNG2-P cell line is heterozygous for the mNG21-10 expression cassette integrated at the AAVS1 safe-harbor locus.

claims.evidence: This is stated in the discussion and shown in the results.

claims.claim: Integration at the AAVS1 locus minimizes the risk of mNG21-10 silencing and provides high and consistent expression across all cells.

claims.evidence: This is supported by a citation to Oceguera-Yanez et al., 2016.

claims.claim: Tagging efficiency with mNG211 in iPSCs ranged from 0.69% to 37.5%.

claims.claim: Tagging efficiency with mNG211 in iPSCs was lower than in mouse embryos (40 to 100% of injected embryos).

claims.claim: Endogenous tagging with mNG211 was overall more efficient than endogenous tagging with full-length mEGFP in iPSCs.

claims.claim: Low endogenous expression levels can limit the detection of tagged proteins by flow cytometry.

claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to Cho et al., 2022; Leonetti et al., 2016; O'Hagan et al., 2021.

claims.claim: The expression levels of 9 mNG211-tagged proteins in iPSCs were consistent with RNA-seq data.

claims.claim: It is unlikely that the mNG211 tag affected the function of the tagged proteins since they showed unique localization patterns consistent with their function.

claims.claim: Nestin and β–3-tubulin were expressed at low levels in undifferentiated iPSCs despite being commonly used as differentiation markers.

claims.claim: The expression of Nestin and β–3-tubulin in some iPS cell lines is consistent with previous reports and published RNA-seq and proteomic data for the 201B7 cell line.
claims.source: This result is consistent with a previous report of their expression in some iPS cell lines (Kuang et al., 2019) and with published RNA-seq and proteomic data for the 201B7 cell line (Iwasaki et al., 2022).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to Kuang et al., 2019 and Iwasaki et al., 2022.

claims.claim: Edited cells had diverse genotypes caused by gene editing, including alleles carrying mutated mNG211 tags and indel mutations.

claims.claim: Clonal isolation provides a more reliable readout of protein expression where variations in signal between cells represent true cell-to-cell variability.
claims.source: Unwanted editing outcomes are ignored when looking at pooled populations, and we recommend isolating and screening clonal cell lines to perform quantitative studies of desired cellular processes, as they provide a more reliable readout of protein expression, where variations in signal between cells within a population represent true cell-to-cell variability.
claims.evidence: This is a recommendation based on the observation of diverse genotypes in edited populations.

claims.claim: iPSCs are programmed to undergo dissociation-induced apoptosis upon loss of attachment or cell-cell contact.
claims.source: Clonal isolation is notoriously inefficient in iPSCs, which are programmed to undergo dissociation-induced apoptosis upon loss of attachment or cell-cell contact (Bhargava et al., 2022; Chen and Pruett-Miller, 2018; Singh, 2019; Tristan et al., 2023; Watanabe et al., 2007).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to Bhargava et al., 2022; Chen and Pruett-Miller, 2018; Singh, 2019; Tristan et al., 2023; Watanabe et al., 2007.

claims.claim: Up to 80% of wells in a 96-well plate showed clonal growth after 10 days using the optimized protocol.
claims.source: We optimized a protocol for efficient single-cell recovery of 201B7 iPSCs after FACS, with up to 80% of wells in a 96-well plate showing clonal growth after 10 days (Figure 3A and Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
claims.evidence: This is shown in Figure 3A and Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claims.claim: mNG21-10/mNG211 complementation is comparable to full-length fluorescent proteins in terms of fluorescence stability and range of expression levels.
claims.source: After clonal isolation, we found that the cells in each edited line had consistent, stable fluorescence. Further, we observed different levels of fluorescence across a range of protein expression levels (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A–T), showing that mNG21-10/mNG211 complementation is comparable to full-length fluorescent proteins.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the observation of stable fluorescence across different expression levels.

claims.claim: The stability of fluorescence levels in endogenously tagged cell lines and the absence of localization artifacts makes this system attractive for quantitative measurements in live cells.
claims.source: Importantly, the stability of fluorescence levels in endogenously tagged cell lines and the absence of localization artifacts compared to over-expressed transgenes makes this system attractive for quantitative measurements in live cells (Husser et al., 2022).
claims.evidence: This is supported by a citation to Husser et al., 2022.

claims.claim: iPSCs are particularly sensitive to phototoxicity compared to other cell types.
claims.source: We found that iPSCs are particularly sensitive to phototoxicity, making it difficult to image weakly expressed endogenous tags over longer periods of time or with short time intervals.
claims.evidence: This is an observation from live imaging experiments.

claims.claim: The sensitivity of iPSCs to phototoxicity has not been previously reported in human or mouse stem cells.
claims.source: This sensitivity has not been previously reported in human or in mouse stem cells, likely because imaging conditions are rarely reported and vary with different setups.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the lack of reports in the literature.

claims.claim: CARE allows cells to be imaged over extended periods of time with high temporal resolution using low exposure settings.
claims.source: With this network, cells can be imaged over extended periods of time with high temporal resolution using low exposure settings, and image files can be restored to generate high-quality movies (Figure 4 and Figure 4—videos 1–6).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated in Figure 4 with comparisons of raw and restored images.

claims.claim: Cytokinesis in live human iPSCs was characterized for the first time in this study.
claims.source: As a proof-of-concept, we characterized cytokinesis in live human iPSCs for the first time.
claims.evidence: This is stated as a novel finding in the manuscript.

claims.claim: Most knowledge of human cell cytokinesis was obtained from studies using HeLa cells.
claims.source: Most of our knowledge of human cell cytokinesis was obtained from studies using HeLa cells, yet the mechanisms regulating this process are expected to vary with cell type (Husser et al., 2022; Ozugergin and Piekny, 2022).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to Husser et al., 2022 and Ozugergin and Piekny, 2022.

claims.claim: The weak central spindle in anaphase iPSCs may explain the broad localization of RhoA compared to HeLa cells.
claims.source: In HeLa cells, the central spindle starts to form immediately after anaphase onset and reaches the cortex by late anaphase (~6 min) (van Oostende Triplet et al., 2014). Thus, the weak central spindle in anaphase iPSCs may explain the broad localization of RhoA (Figure 5G–H).
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on comparison to HeLa cells and supported by a citation to van Oostende Triplet et al., 2014.

claims.claim: Astral microtubules extending to the cortex in the equatorial region could restrict anillin localization in iPSCs.
claims.source: In iPSCs, the astral microtubules extended to the cortex in the equatorial region, which could restrict anillin localization.
claims.evidence: This is speculation based on the observation of astral microtubules and narrow anillin localization.

claims.claim: Perturbations that cause an increase in astral microtubules decrease the breadth of anillin in HeLa cells.
claims.source: In HeLa cells, we previously showed that perturbations that cause an increase in astral microtubules decreases the breadth of anillin (van Oostende Triplet et al., 2014).
claims.evidence: This is supported by a citation to van Oostende Triplet et al., 2014.

claims.claim: Interactions with other proteins or phospholipids could further restrict the localization of anillin in iPSCs.
claims.source: However, interactions with other proteins or phospholipids could further restrict the localization of anillin in iPSCs (Ozugergin and Piekny, 2022).
claims.evidence: This is speculation supported by a citation to Ozugergin and Piekny, 2022.

claims.claim: The findings reveal how cytokinesis occurs in a non-transformed human stem cell and provide a framework to reveal how mechanisms vary with different cell types.
claims.source: Thus our findings reveal how cytokinesis occurs in a non-transformed human stem cell, and provide a framework to reveal how the mechanisms controlling cytokinesis vary with different cell types in an isogenic context.
claims.evidence: This is a summary of the significance of the findings.

claims.claim: High transfection and editing efficiencies can be achieved in iPSCs by using electroporation and delivering Cas9/sgRNA RNP complexes instead of plasmids.
claims.source: High transfection and editing efficiencies can be achieved in iPSCs by using electroporation and delivering Cas9/sgRNA RNP complexes instead of plasmids (Kim et al., 2014; Liang et al., 2015).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to Kim et al., 2014 and Liang et al., 2015.

claims.claim: Tagging efficiency is increased by using NHEJ inhibitors.
claims.source: Tagging efficiency is further increased by using NHEJ inhibitors (Chu et al., 2015; Maruyama et al., 2015; Maurissen and Woltjen, 2020; Schimmel et al., 2023).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to Chu et al., 2015; Maruyama et al., 2015; Maurissen and Woltjen, 2020; Schimmel et al., 2023.

claims.claim: This work provides the basis for a high-quality endogenous tag library in human iPSCs.
claims.source: Altogether, this work provides the basis for a high-quality endogenous tag library in human iPSCs, which will be used to study protein function in human stem cells and across human cell types in vitro.
claims.evidence: This is a summary of the significance and future applications of the work.

results.result: The authors generated and validated the smNG2-P iPSC line by integrating an mNG21-10 expression cassette at the AAVS1 locus in 201B7 iPSCs. The cell line was extensively validated for correct integration, absence of off-target effects, normal karyotype, pluripotency markers, differentiation capacity, and functional complementation with mNG211.
results.evaluation: Claims C22-C35 and C66-C67 collectively demonstrate comprehensive validation of the smNG2-P cell line. The data includes sequencing confirmation (C28), digital PCR for copy number (C29), off-target analysis (C30), karyotyping (C31), pluripotency marker expression (C32-C33), differentiation capacity (C33), mycoplasma testing (C34), and functional complementation (C35). The integration strategy using AAVS1 locus is well-justified by citations (C25, C67).

results.result: The smNG2-P cell line enables efficient endogenous tagging with mNG211 across 17 genes with variable efficiency (0.69-37.5%). Tagged proteins showed expected localization patterns and fluorescence intensities correlated with RNA-seq expression data, though detection of weakly expressed proteins was limited by flow cytometry sensitivity.
results.evaluation: Claims C2, C23, C36-C43, and C68-C73 demonstrate successful endogenous tagging with comprehensive characterization. The variable tagging efficiency is documented (C38, C68), fluorescence correlates with expression levels (C40, C72), and localization patterns are consistent with known protein functions (C39-C43, C73). Comparisons to other systems (C69-C70) and limitations (C71) are appropriately acknowledged. The data is supported by Nanopore sequencing, flow cytometry, and microscopy.

results.result: The authors developed protocols for efficient single-cell isolation by FACS (61.4% average recovery, up to 80%) and screening by Nanopore sequencing, revealing diverse genotypes in edited populations that warrant clonal isolation for quantitative studies.
results.evaluation: Claims C24, C44-C47, C76, C79-C81 demonstrate successful protocol development with quantitative recovery data (C44, C81). The observation of diverse genotypes (C45, C76) is well-documented and appropriately leads to the recommendation for clonal isolation (C79). The challenge of iPSC single-cell recovery is acknowledged with appropriate citations (C80). The protocols address a known bottleneck in iPSC gene editing.

results.result: iPSCs exhibit high sensitivity to phototoxicity during live imaging, requiring low-exposure settings that produce low signal-to-noise images. The authors demonstrate that CARE neural network-based image restoration enables high-quality timelapse imaging of weakly expressed endogenous tags with high temporal resolution.
results.evaluation: Claims C3, C50-C54, C84-C86 demonstrate a critical technical advance. The phototoxicity sensitivity is documented (C50-C51, C84), signal-to-noise limitations are quantified (C52), and CARE restoration is shown to dramatically improve image quality (C54, C86). The approach is validated across multiple cell lines (C53-C54). This represents an important methodological contribution for live imaging of iPSCs, though the claim of novelty regarding phototoxicity sensitivity (C85) is speculative.

results.result: The authors characterized cytokinesis in live human iPSCs for the first time, measuring contractile ring ingression duration (18.6±4.0 min), protein localization dynamics, and spatial distributions of anillin and RhoA. iPSCs show distinct features including a poorly-organized central spindle and prominent astral microtubules.
results.evaluation: Claims C55-C63, C87-C88 provide the first quantitative characterization of cytokinesis in live human iPSCs. The measurements are precise with error estimates (C55, C59-C60), timing is documented (C57-C58), and comparisons to other cell types are made (C63). The observations of central spindle organization (C61) and astral microtubules (C62) are supported by microscopy data. This represents a novel contribution to understanding cytokinesis in non-transformed human cells.

results.result: The authors propose that the weak central spindle in iPSCs explains the broad RhoA localization, while prominent astral microtubules may restrict anillin to a narrow zone. These findings reveal cell-type-specific differences in cytokinesis mechanisms compared to HeLa cells.
results.evaluation: Claims C64, C89-C90, C92 are speculative interpretations supported by correlative observations and citations to HeLa cell studies (C65, C91). While the observations of weak central spindle (C61) and narrow anillin localization (C59) are well-documented, the mechanistic links are inferred rather than directly tested. The interpretations are reasonable and supported by prior work in other systems, but would require experimental manipulation to confirm causality. Claim C93 appropriately frames these as initial findings requiring further investigation.

results.result: The mNG21-10/mNG211 complementation system shows efficient fluorescence reconstitution across a range of protein expression levels, with stable fluorescence in clonal lines comparable to full-length fluorescent proteins, making it suitable for quantitative live cell measurements.
results.evaluation: Claims C48, C82-C83 are supported by observations of fluorescence in both weakly (anillin) and strongly (RhoA) expressed proteins (C46-C47), stable fluorescence across clonal lines, and appropriate localization patterns (C49, C73). The comparison to full-length fluorescent proteins is supported by citation (C83). The inference is reasonable based on the presented data.

results.result: Nestin and β-3-tubulin were unexpectedly expressed at low levels in undifferentiated iPSCs despite being commonly used as differentiation markers, consistent with previous reports for the 201B7 cell line.
results.evaluation: Claims C74-C75 report an interesting observation supported by the authors' data (Figure 2) and corroborated by citations to prior RNA-seq and proteomic studies (C75). This represents a minor but valid finding about marker expression variability in iPSC lines.

results.result: The authors speculate that single-nucleotide mutations may arise from ssODN synthesis errors, while ssODN rearrangements could result from microhomologies or NHEJ/HDR repair mechanisms.
results.evaluation: Claims C77-C78 are explicitly speculative (C77) or supported only by citation to prior work (C78). While the speculation is reasonable given the observed genotypic diversity (C45, C76), no direct evidence is provided to test these hypotheses. These represent plausible explanations requiring further investigation.

results.result: The work provides a foundation for generating a high-quality endogenous tag library in human iPSCs by combining established approaches including electroporation, RNP delivery, NHEJ inhibitors, and the split mNeonGreen system.
results.evaluation: Claims C94-C96 appropriately summarize the significance and future potential of the work. The technical approaches are supported by citations (C94-C95), and the conclusion (C96) is justified by the demonstrated feasibility across multiple genes and the developed protocols. This represents a reasonable assessment of the work's contribution and future applications.

results.result: The introduction provides context on fluorescent protein tagging, endogenous tagging advantages, split mNeonGreen system properties, and the rationale for studying iPSCs, all supported by appropriate citations to prior work.
results.evaluation: Claims C1, C4-C21 represent background information and context appropriately supported by citations to prior literature. These claims establish the scientific foundation and rationale for the study. The characterization of the split mNeonGreen system (C11-C15) and iPSC properties (C17-C21) are well-documented in the cited literature.

results.result: The smNG2-P parental iPSC line was generated by integrating mNG21-10 at the AAVS1 locus in 201B7 iPSCs and was extensively validated for single-copy integration, normal karyotype, pluripotency markers, differentiation capacity, off-target effects, and functional complementation with mNG211.
results.evaluation: Reviewer 1 explicitly states 'Characterization of the mNG2 tagged parental iPSC line was well and carefully done including validation of a single integration, the presence of markers for continued pluripotency, selected off-target analysis and G-banding-based structural rearrangement detection.' The first editor also affirms 'the methods are solid, and the data presented support the authors' conclusions.' Reviewer 1 raises a minor concern about NCAM as a mesoderm marker, but the authors' response is accepted ('fine').

results.result: Multiple genes (17 total) were efficiently targeted for endogenous tagging with mNG211 in the smNG2-P cell line, with tagging efficiencies ranging from 0.69% to 37.5%, and fluorescence intensity correlating with expected expression levels for 9 proteins expressed in iPSCs.
results.evaluation: Reviewer 1 acknowledges 'The ability to tag proteins with simple ssODNs in iPSC capable of multi-lineage differentiation will undoubtedly be useful' but raises concerns about lack of quantification and validation: 'IF and flow cytometry figures lack quantification and information on replication. How consistent is the brightness and localization of the markers?' and 'The localization of markers, while consistent with expectations, is not validated by a second technique such as antibody staining.' Reviewer 3 criticizes 'The fluorescence intensity of the split mNeonGreen appears rather low... For low expression targets this is an important limitation.' While authors added quantification in response, Reviewer 1 notes 'it would have been fairly simple to do for at least a handful of markers, image, fix and stain to demonstrate unequivocally the tag and protein are co-localized.'

results.result: Protocols were developed for efficient single-cell isolation by FACS (61.4% average recovery, up to 80%) and screening by Nanopore sequencing, revealing diverse genotypes in edited clones including correctly tagged, mutated, and indel alleles, warranting clonal isolation for quantitative studies.
results.evaluation: Reviewer 1 explicitly states 'Validation of clone genotypes was carefully performed and highlights the continued need for caution with regards to editing outcomes.' The first editor affirms 'the methods are solid, and the data presented support the authors' conclusions.' No reviewer challenges the clonal isolation methodology or genotyping results.

results.result: Tagged proteins (H2B, actin, tubulin, anillin, RhoA) showed expected localization patterns consistent with their function, with stable fluorescence across different expression levels, indicating the mNG211 tag likely does not affect protein function and is comparable to full-length fluorescent proteins.
results.evaluation: Reviewer 1 notes 'The localization of markers, while consistent with expectations, is not validated by a second technique such as antibody staining' and later states 'There was no question that the localization fit with expectations, however, this still doesn't show that in the same cell the tag is in the same spot. It would have been fairly simple to do for at least a handful of markers, image, fix and stain to demonstrate unequivocally the tag and protein are co-localized.' While the first editor accepts the conclusions, the lack of orthogonal validation creates uncertainty about whether the tag truly reports endogenous protein behavior.

results.result: iPSCs are particularly sensitive to phototoxicity, requiring low-exposure imaging settings that produce low signal-to-noise ratios. A CARE neural network was trained to restore low-exposure images, drastically improving signal-to-noise ratio and enabling extended live imaging of cytokinesis.
results.evaluation: Reviewer 1 raises significant concerns about the CARE approach: 'The AI-based signal to noise enhancement needs more details and testing. Such models can introduce strong assumptions and thus artefacts into the resolved data.' The reviewer specifically asks whether the model could 'introduce artefacts where it forces signal localization to those areas even for others' and requests validation with 'scrambled pixel locations' or 'markers with different localization from the training set.' The authors' response that they 'did not try to restore scrambled images or images of mismatched markers' is deemed inadequate: 'I do not feel this comment has been in any way adequately addressed.' Reviewer 3 also notes 'image restoration could not be the best solution since a lot of biologically relevant information will be lost anyway.'

results.result: Cytokinesis was characterized in live human iPSCs for the first time, revealing that anillin accumulates at the equatorial cortex ~4 min after anaphase onset forming a narrow peak (4.1±0.7 μm), RhoA accumulates by ~6 min with broader localization (6.6±2.2 μm), ingression duration is 18.6±4.0 min, and iPSCs have a poorly-organized central spindle with strong astral microtubules, which may explain the broad RhoA localization and restricted anillin localization.
results.evaluation: The first editor states 'the methods are solid, and the data presented support the authors' conclusions' and 'these methodologies should be useful to a wide audience of cell biologists.' Reviewer 4 notes 'Overall the tools and resources reported in this paper will be valuable for the community that aims to study proteins at endogenous levels.' While Reviewer 1's concerns about CARE validation create uncertainty about image restoration methodology, no reviewer directly challenges the cytokinesis findings themselves or the biological interpretations.

results.result: Background claims about fluorescent protein tagging, CRISPR/Cas9 editing, split mNeonGreen system properties, iPSCs, and cytokinesis knowledge from the literature are cited to establish context for the study.
results.evaluation: These are background/contextual claims supported by citations. No reviewer challenges these established facts or literature citations. They provide the scientific foundation for the work but are not novel findings of this study.

results.result: Supporting observations and interpretations include that complementation occurs efficiently over a range of expression levels, Nestin and β3-tubulin are expressed at low levels in undifferentiated iPSCs, mutations may arise from ssODN synthesis or repair mechanisms, and this work provides the basis for a high-quality endogenous tag library in human iPSCs.
results.evaluation: These are supporting observations and interpretations that reviewers do not challenge. Reviewer 3 notes the work is 'extremely incremental, no improvements are present in the split-Fluorescent (split-FP) protein variant used nor in the approach for endogenous tagging with split-FPs' and questions 'what the advantages of the system are,' but this critiques novelty rather than the validity of these specific claims. The first editor and Reviewer 4 affirm the value of the tools and resources.

comparisons.comparison: Perfect agreement. Both evaluations find the smNG2-P cell line characterization well-supported, including validation of single integration, pluripotency markers, off-target analysis, and karyotyping (C22-C35, C66-C67). Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Perfect agreement. Both evaluations find the clonal isolation protocols and genotype validation well-supported (C24, C44-C47, C76, C79-C81). Both acknowledge the careful documentation of diverse genotypes and rate as SUPPORTED.

Significant disagreement. OpenEval rates endogenous tagging characterization as SUPPORTED (C2, C23, C36-C43, C68-C72), while peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN due to lack of quantification, insufficient replication information, and absence of orthogonal validation (e.g., antibody co-staining). Peer reviewers also note low fluorescence intensity concerns (C73 not in peer result).

Major disagreement. OpenEval rates CARE image restoration as SUPPORTED with only minor speculation concerns (C3, C50-C54, C84-C86), while peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN with significant concerns about potential AI-introduced artifacts, inadequate validation testing, and loss of biologically relevant information.

Agreement on background claims. Both evaluations find the literature-based background and contextual information well-supported by citations (C1, C4-C21 in OpenEval; subset plus C65, C94-C95 in peer review). Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Partial overlap with different scope. OpenEval R5 focuses on cytokinesis measurements (C55-C63, C87-C88) rated SUPPORTED. Peer R6 includes these claims plus mechanistic interpretations (C89-C93), all rated SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers accept both the measurements and interpretations despite CARE methodology concerns raised elsewhere.

Disagreement on certainty level. OpenEval rates mechanistic interpretations about cytokinesis as UNCERTAIN (C64, C89-C93), noting they are speculative and correlative. Peer reviewers include these claims in their SUPPORTED evaluation (R6), accepting the interpretations alongside the measurements.

Disagreement on protein localization validation. OpenEval rates claims about proper protein localization as SUPPORTED (C48, C82-C83). Peer R4 rates related localization claims (C49, C73, C82-C83) as UNCERTAIN, emphasizing lack of orthogonal validation via antibody co-staining.

Agreement on minor findings. Both evaluations find the observation about marker expression variability (C74-C75) supported by data and citations. Both rate as SUPPORTED, though peer review groups with other minor claims (C48, C77-C78, C96).

Disagreement on speculation. OpenEval rates explanations for genotypic diversity as UNCERTAIN (C77-C78), noting they are explicitly speculative. Peer reviewers include these in SUPPORTED evaluation (R8), not challenging the speculative interpretations.

Partial overlap on significance claims. OpenEval R10 addresses future potential and significance (C94-C96) rated SUPPORTED. Peer R7 includes C94-C95 among background/contextual claims also rated SUPPORTED. Minor overlap with peer R8 on C96.

Minimal overlap. OpenEval R10 includes conclusion about future applications (C96) rated SUPPORTED. Peer R8 also includes C96 among supporting observations rated SUPPORTED, though grouped with different claims (C48, C74-C75, C77-C78).
